breaks.why: WordPress's PCRE runs out of JIT stack (or pcre.backtrack_limit) on this content, preg_replace_callback() returns null and do_shortcode() returns "" (with a strtr() deprecation). The port's scanners cannot fail this way and return the real result. Deliberate difference 1 of the shortcode design.

After setlocale( LC_CTYPE, a Latin-1 locale ), PHP's PCRE builds locale tables and \w matches 0xE9, so WordPress leaves "[a\xE9]" alone. The port always uses the C locale's classes and expands it. Deliberate difference 2 of the shortcode design. Because the port expands it, its attribute text "\xE9" also raises WordPress's invalid-UTF-8 deprecation, which the later steps' notices carry.
